body: The US Air Force has awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract to produce and field the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW), the Department of the Air Force announced on October 26, 2026. The contract had been awarded on September 29, 2026, under the Department of War's Enterprise-Wide Agile Acquisition Contract. Citing operational security, the department did not disclose how many weapons were ordered or when deliveries would begin. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink described ARRW as a turning point and as a high-speed weapon able to penetrate advanced air defenses.

Lockheed Martin confirmed the contract on October 27, 2026, as it broke ground on an expansion of Building P-20 in Troy, Alabama, adding about 4,370 square meters (47,000 square feet) and tripling the existing production area there, with jobs expected over the next four years. The company said it had already funded preparation work, including $67 million for the expansion and equipment, within a broader investment of $8 billion to $9 billion planned through 2030 to meet munitions demand. Its hypersonic assembly facility in Courtland, Alabama, opened in October 2021, supports ARRW alongside the US Navy's Conventional Prompt Strike and the US Army's Long Range Hypersonic Weapon programs.

ARRW is a boost-glide weapon designed to strike high-value targets from standoff range: a solid-fuel booster accelerates it beyond Mach 5 before releasing a maneuvering glide vehicle, and it is integrated on the B-52 Stratofortress. The program's path to production was troubled: after three unsuccessful tests in 2021, it achieved its first successful booster test on May 14, 2022, and the first launch of a full operational prototype from a B-52H on December 9, 2022. The Air Force abandoned procurement plans in 2023 in favor of the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile (HACM), and the fiscal 2025 budget request released in March 2024 included no ARRW procurement funding. On June 5, 2025, however, then-Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin told the House Armed Services Committee that the fiscal 2026 request would include ARRW funding. The Air Force is now pursuing two distinct air-launched hypersonic weapons: the rocket-boosted ARRW and the scramjet-powered HACM.
en.summary: The US Air Force has awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract to produce and field the AGM-183A ARRW hypersonic weapon, reviving a boost-glide program that suffered three failed tests in 2021 and was nearly abandoned in 2023 in favor of the HACM.
en.title: US Air Force puts Lockheed Martin's troubled hypersonic ARRW into production

body: 美國空軍部10月26日宣布，已授予洛克希德馬丁一份6.94億美元合約，生產並部署AGM-183A空射快速反應武器（ARRW）。這份合約實際上已在9月29日授出，屬於美國戰爭部的全企業敏捷採購合約；空軍部基於作戰安全考量，沒有公布採購數量與開始交付的時間。空軍部長Troy Meink表示，ARRW象徵一個轉折點，是一款能以高速穿透先進防空系統的武器。

洛克希德馬丁10月27日證實這份合約，同日在阿拉巴馬州Troy為P-20大樓擴建工程動土，擴建面積約4370平方公尺（4萬7000平方英尺），讓當地現有生產面積擴大為三倍，未來四年可望帶來就業機會。該公司表示已先行投入準備資金，其中6700萬美元用於擴建與設備，屬於其因應彈藥需求、規劃至2030年投入80億至90億美元投資的一部分。洛克希德馬丁2021年10月在阿拉巴馬州Courtland啟用的極音速組裝廠，也同時支援ARRW以及美國海軍的傳統快速打擊與陸軍的長程極音速武器計畫。

ARRW是一種助推滑翔武器，用於在防區外打擊高價值目標：固體燃料助推器先把武器加速到超過5馬赫，再釋放可機動的滑翔體，並整合在B-52同溫層堡壘轟炸機上。它的量產之路並不順遂：2021年三度試射失敗，2022年5月14日才首次成功完成助推器試射，同年12月9日首次由B-52H發射全功能原型；2023年空軍一度放棄採購計畫，轉向極音速攻擊巡弋飛彈（HACM），2024年3月公布的2025財政年度預算需求也沒有編列ARRW的採購經費。不過時任空軍參謀長David Allvin在2025年6月5日告訴眾議院軍事委員會，2026財政年度需求將納入ARRW經費。隨著量產合約授出，美國空軍將同時推進兩條空射極音速路線：火箭助推的ARRW與衝壓噴射動力的HACM。
zh.summary: 美國空軍授予洛克希德馬丁6.94億美元合約，生產並部署AGM-183A空射快速反應武器（ARRW）極音速飛彈；這款曾三度試射失敗、2023年一度被放棄採購的助推滑翔武器，在沉寂數年後正式重返量產。
